slides.title: Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity for Real-Time Online Motor Learning in Physical Human-Robot Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME ONLINE MOTOR LEARNING VIA FREE-ENERGY-GATED PLASTICITY
slides.highlight: This work introduces Free-Energy-Gated Plasticity (FEGP) to enable robots to acquire and retain motor patterns during real-time physical interaction, supporting RwB's focus on embodied learning and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: FEGP enables robots to learn multiple motor patterns online without forgetting, using free energy to regulate plasticity.
card.key_idea: A sigmoidal plasticity gate scales synaptic updates based on variational free energy, increasing learning during model-environment mismatch and suppressing it when predictions are accurate.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 10 randomized teaching streams and physical human-robot interaction. Metrics included repertoire coverage, retention, and DTW shape distance; results showed significant improvement over constant rates.
card.limitation: The method relies on a sliding window of recent observations, which may limit long-term memory without further architectural extensions.

slides.title: A Tendon-Driven Five-Fingered Hand with Distributed Tactile Perception for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: DEXTEROUS FIVE-FINGERED HAND WITH TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tendon-driven five-fingered hand with a soft-rigid-hybrid structure and dual-modality tactile sensing. It is relevant to RwB for its application of embodied AI to complex humanoid manipulations and tactile perception.

card.one_liner: A tendon-driven five-fingered robotic hand featuring a soft-rigid-hybrid structure and distributed dual-modality tactile sensing.
card.key_idea: A hybrid structure combining compliance and force, integrated with tactile sensors on distal and middle phalanges for static and dynamic force detection.
card.evaluation: Feasibility demonstrated via manipulation experiments: counting gestures, finger-to-thumb pinching, object grasping, and bottle-grasp tactile recording.

slides.title: TacForcing: Streaming Action Generation with Execution-Time Tactile Feedback
slides.tldr: STREAMING ACTION GENERATION WITH TACTILE FEEDBACK
slides.highlight: TacForcing introduces a streaming action-generation framework and Execution-Aware Tactile Attention to incorporate real-time tactile feedback into contact-rich manipulation.

card.one_liner: TacForcing enables contact-rich manipulation by incorporating real-time tactile feedback into streaming action generation.
card.key_idea: A Streaming Action Expert generates action blocks progressively, using Execution-Aware Tactile Attention (EATA) to condition only the next scheduled block on current tactile updates.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on six UniVTAC simulated tasks and three real-world tasks against VLA baselines; achieved average success rates of 65% and 69% respectively.

slides.title: Robust Slip Detection and Material Classification via Spatiotemporal Transformers on a Uniformly-Illuminated Visuo-Tactile Sensor
slides.tldr: SPATIOTEMPORAL TRANSFORMERS FOR VISUO-TACTILE SLIP DETECTION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a visuo-tactile sensor and a dual-head TimeSformer network capable of high-accuracy contact state prediction and fine-grained slip direction classification.

card.one_liner: A marker-less visuo-tactile sensor and framework for high-precision 3D reconstruction, slip detection, and material classification.
card.key_idea: Combines a uniform RGB illumination sensor with a dual-head TimeSformer for spatiotemporal slip tracking and a ResNet-50 for static material recognition.
card.evaluation: Tested on 15 objects; achieved 95.5% state and 91.5% direction accuracy on unseen objects, and 98.8% material classification accuracy.

slides.title: VISTA: Visually Inferred Spatial ConTact Attention for Contact-Rich Manipulation
slides.tldr: VISUALLY INFERRED CONTACT FEEDBACK FOR MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: VISTA-Policy uses a Visual Deformation Field to provide high-dimensional visuo-physical feedback for contact-rich tasks without requiring dedicated tactile sensors.

card.one_liner: VISTA enables contact-rich robot manipulation by using external cameras to infer gripper deformation as tactile feedback.
card.key_idea: A framework extracting a 3D Visual Deformation Field (VDF) from compliant grippers, using energy-based denoising and a relative incremental action space for adaptive, contact-aware control.
card.evaluation: Tested on grasping, unscrewing, and calligraphy tasks against DP3 and tactile baselines. Results show superior success rates, sample efficiency, and OOD scale generalization.
card.limitation: Requires a compliant gripper whose structural deformation remains observable from an external camera.

slides.title: One-Shot Learning from Demonstration of Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation by Identifying Physical Interactions
slides.highlight: This work proposes an LfD method that explicitly models physical interactions and uses a hybrid position-force controller, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics/force-based skill acquisition and adaptive AI coaching.

card.one_liner: A one-shot LfD method for contact-rich manipulation using explicit physical interaction modeling.
card.key_idea: A hybrid position-force controller tracks trajectories and triggers transitions based on identified contact-based conditions extracted from a single human demonstration.
card.evaluation: Real robot experiments on doors, locks, bolt screwing, dislodging, and contouring; demonstrated robustness to geometric variations and online adaptation.

slides.authors: A. H. G. Overbeek et al.

slides.title: VT-MUSE: Multimodal Unified Sequential Visuotactile Representation Learning for Manipulation
slides.highlight: VT-MUSE utilizes cross-modal temporal alignment and a conditional variational latent model to capture fine-grained dependencies between visual and tactile observations, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception.

card.one_liner: VT-MUSE learns unified sequential visuotactile representations to improve contact-rich robotic manipulation in simulation and real-world.
card.key_idea: A two-stage framework: Stage I aligns modalities via temporal contrast; Stage II uses a conditional variational model to reconstruct masked vision and predict tactile depth changes.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on UniVTAC simulation and physical robot tasks. Outperformed baselines by 16.25 percentage points in simulation and achieved 95% success rate on physical tasks.
card.limitation: Uses fixed sampling strides and window sizes; pretraining scaled to only 7 tasks, leaving broader scaling laws unvalidated.

slides.title: Leveraging Inter-object Affordances for Efficient Planning in Contact-rich Tasks
slides.highlight: This research introduces a method using Vision-Language Models to generate inter-object affordance abstractions, significantly improving success rates and planning speed for complex robotic interactions.

card.one_liner: U-TAMP leverages symbolic inter-object affordances to efficiently plan contact-rich robotic tasks with heterogeneous objects.
card.key_idea: Extends Unified TAMP by using VLMs to generate symbolic abstractions of physical interaction constraints (grasping, supporting, lifting, sliding) to guide PDDL-based heuristic search.
card.evaluation: Simulated kitchen organization tasks (2-5 objects) in CoppeliaSim. Compared against original U-TAMP and VLM-based planners using success rate and planning time.
card.limitation: Task success is highly sensitive to affordance detection accuracy; a few incorrect assignments can render stacking unfeasible.
